carousel.title: 1. Overview
carousel.heading: $163.6M mixed-use redevelopment in Bricktown OKC
carousel.content:
OKCIAN Origin (O2) + Spaghetti Block Redevelopment
Bricktown, Oklahoma City, OK

A $163.6M mixed-use urban redevelopment - four towers, 383,000+ sq. ft., five capital sources. We structured the deal, built the financial model, secured public financing commitments, and produced the investor materials that got a first-time developer to the table with institutional equity.

carousel.title: 2. Details
carousel.heading: Project at a glance
carousel.content:
- Total Development Cost: $163.6M
- Equity Raise: $25M
- Levered IRR: 21.3% | Equity Multiple: 3.95x
- Program: Hotel, multifamily (155 units), retail, museum, restaurant, structured parking
- Location: Sheridan Ave & Main St, Bricktown OKC - Opportunity Zone
- Status: TIF commitment secured; land under contract (Q2 2025)

carousel.title: 3. The Situation
carousel.heading: A rare site, a credibility gap, and a closing window
carousel.content:
BG Infinity Capital identified a full city block in Oklahoma City's Bricktown district - the historic Spaghetti Warehouse and surrounding surface lots - sitting at the intersection of an expiring TIF district, an Opportunity Zone designation, and a rapidly developing urban core.

The opportunity was real. But the sponsor team was a first-time large-scale developer with no institutional track record. The existing Downtown TIF district was expiring in 2026. And closing a five-source capital stack - HUD, TIF, C-PACE, Opportunity Zone equity, and traditional debt - required navigating five counterparties with five different underwriting timelines simultaneously.

Without the right financial infrastructure and public benefit narrative, the deal would stall before it reached the market.

carousel.title: 4. The Ask
carousel.heading: Build everything needed to close a $163M deal from scratch
carousel.content:
The sponsor came in with a vision, a site, and a team. They needed:

- A master financial model that could withstand HUD underwriting, city TIF review, and institutional investor due diligence - simultaneously
- A capital stack structured across five sources without any one of them collapsing the others
- A government relations strategy to create a brand-new TIF district in under 12 months
- An investor pitch that told a credible story despite an acknowledged lack of development experience
- A floor-by-floor program that aligned with the financial projections - so the architecture and the proforma told the same story

carousel.title: 5. The Approach
carousel.heading: Three parallel tracks, one integrated strategy
carousel.content:
We ran the financial, public finance, and investor communications workstreams simultaneously rather than sequentially - because the TIF timeline, the equity raise, and the HUD application could not wait on each other.

The core strategic decision was to convert the landowner of the Spaghetti Warehouse from a cash seller into an equity partner. This reduced required outside equity by $8M, aligned long-term incentives, and strengthened the project's credibility with both city stakeholders and institutional investors.

On the public financing side, we framed the project's government case not as a subsidy request but as a catalyst investment - translating the development's economics into a 25-year, $2.53B regional impact argument that gave Alliance for Economic Development leadership what they needed to move toward formal approval.

On the investor side, we made a deliberate choice to name the sponsor's inexperience as a risk - then answered it structurally. Sophisticated investors distrust materials that show only upside.

carousel.title: 6. The Work
carousel.heading: Four workstreams, one integrated package
carousel.content:
Financial Modeling
Built a 14-tab master developer proforma across four independent towers - each with its own operating statement, cash flow model, and capital assumptions - rolled into a consolidated returns analysis. Unlevered IRR: 16.1%. Levered IRR: 21.3%. TIF toggle built into the assumptions tab so any counterparty could scenario-test in real time.

Capital Stack Architecture
Structured a five-source, $163.6M stack: $49M HUD 221(d)(4), $32.5M TIF/C-PACE, $24.4M traditional debt, $15M Opportunity Zone equity, $10M sponsor, $8M landowner conversion. Each source sequenced to the others' underwriting timelines.

Public Finance Navigation
Submitted a proforma to the Alliance for Economic Development of Oklahoma City sufficient to trigger a formal TIF framework letter - structured as a 10-year ad valorem reimbursement with phased rates across all four towers. New TIF district creation initiated concurrently with EDA approval process.

Investor Pitch Development
Produced a 22-slide investor deck built to work for three audiences at once: private equity, city stakeholders, and development partners. Included property cashflow projections, entity structure diagrams, market outlook, risk/mitigation matrix, and a 25-year economic impact analysis.

carousel.title: 7. The Impact
carousel.heading: What moved because of this work
carousel.content:
- TIF framework letter secured from the Alliance for Economic Development of Oklahoma City - April 2025. A government body reviewed the proforma and responded with a structured reimbursement framework before a single shovel hit the ground.
- Spaghetti Warehouse placed under contract - February 2025. The seller converted to an equity partner, removing $8M from the required equity raise.
- Equity negotiations active with remaining landowners and target LP roster.
- Architecture and engineering on track for Q3 2025 completion.
- Groundbreaking projected Q4 2025.
- Projected 25-year economic impact to the Bricktown district: $2.53B.

carousel.title: 8. The Deliverables
carousel.heading: What we produced
carousel.content:
- Master Developer Proforma - 14-tab XLSX model with four-tower rollup, TIF toggle, dual return analysis, and 317,000+ sq. ft. rent roll
- Investor Pitch Deck - 22-slide PDF covering vision, capital stack, financials, team, market outlook, risks, and next steps
- Capital Stack Memo - Five-source structure with sequenced underwriting strategy and landowner conversion framework
- TIF Submission Package - Pro forma and public benefit narrative submitted to the Alliance for Economic Development; resulted in a signed preliminary framework letter
- Floor-by-Floor Architectural Program - 15-level area schedule (Levels B-15) coordinated with proforma rent roll assumptions
- Tower Blocking Diagrams - Four-phase massing studies (North, South, East, West towers) with color-coded use program
- Architectural Renderings - Five-perspective visual set for investor and city presentation use
